research_keywords: glomerulonephritis | kidney failure | human leukocyte antigen (HLA) | autoimmunity | regulatory T cells
description: Glomerulonephritis (GN), a common cause of kidney failure, usually results from an immune system attack on the kidneys. Current treatments suppress the whole immune system, making patients vulnerable to infection. We aim to harness the body’s protective immune cells (Tregs) as a potential GN treatment. description: Neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) are uncommon cancers. description: There’s recent evidence that children get leaner and fitter during the school term, but become fatter and less fit over the summer holidays. description: During embryogenesis genes are switched on and off by a variety of molecular mechanisms. One such gene-silencing mechanism is DNA methylation. This chemical modification mostly targets germline-specific genes in early embryos. In adults, the loss of this mark and the reactivation of this set of genes has been observed in many cancers including melanoma, hepatic and lung cancer. description: Advanced Glycation Endproducts (AGEs) are formed when sugars and proteins stick together, resulting in the brown colour, caramel flavour and sticky surface of heated foods. description: CADASIL is a cerebral small vessel disease which is one of the most common heritable cause of stroke and vascular dementia in adults. research_keywords: malaria | malaria control | malaria drug resistance | mechanism of action | plasmodium
description: Antibiotics that kill bacteria have been successfully repurposed to kill the parasites that cause malaria, and are now important elements in malaria control and elimination. description: Sepsis is overwhelming reaction to severe infection. Patients with haematological malignancy (blood cancers) have reduced immunity to infection and many develop sepsis. research_keywords: antimicrobial resistance | bacteriophage | combination therapy | urinary tract infection (uti) | pneumonia
description: The control of bacterial infections is perhaps the most important achievement of modern medicine. However, we have failed to keep pace with microbes becoming increasingly resistant to available antimicrobials. One of the most promising strategies is to use viruses that can selectively infect and kill bacterial cells, and to give these viruses as treatment in combination with antimicrobials.

title: Revitalising the Antifungal Pipeline with Transition Metals
source_grant_title: Revitalising the Antifungal Pipeline with Transition Metals
research_keywords: antifungal | fungal infection | in vivo | drug development | fungi
description: This project delves into the potential ability of metal-containing compounds to kill deadly fungi. Using new techniques and adapting machine learning approaches, we will create and test thousands of metal compounds to see if any are effective against fungal infections. This work could lead to the development of much-needed new treatments for stubborn fungal infections.

description: Too much salt in the diet is a main cause of high blood pressure, stroke, heart attack and kidney failure.
